note: Section 4.4.1: "Every SPD SHOULD have a nominal, final entry that matches anything that is otherwise unmatched, and discards it." Re-judged 2026-11-08 (independent auditor) after the row gained {partial}, the fix the previous weak verdict asked for. Tested: "a nominal, final entry that matches anything that is otherwise unmatched, and discards it", in the XFRM SPDs the IKE engine owns. Node-wide if_id 0 SPD: TestRFC4301DefaultFinalSPDEntryDiscards (installUnmatched builds in/out/fwd wildcard DISCARD at PriorityUnmatched by default), TestRFC4301FinalEntryIsUnderEveryZeSPDEntry (every write replayed, catch-all present and DISCARD whenever another Ze entry is live), negative TestRFC4301InboundClearPacketIsDiscardedByTheDefaultFinalEntry (kernel XfrmInPolBlock +1, packet not delivered). Per-interface if_id SPDs: TestInterfaceSPDCatchAllEntries (interfaceSPDCatchAll: DISCARD at the if_id, below PriorityChildSA, unnarrowed), TestApplyInstallsInterfaceSPDCatchAllAndGuard, TestReleaseRemovesInterfaceSPDAndGuard, TestRFC4301InterfaceSPDDiscardsUnmatchedInKernel (XfrmOutPolBlock rises at the if_id, Child SA policy outranks it), negative TestInterfaceSPDCatchAllInstallFailureFailsTheApply. Tagged units unchanged since the previous judgement; they assert the exact DISCARD action and ranking, not a floor. Gap: "Every SPD". Checked at the producers and accurate: internal/component/ike/dataplane/vpp_policy.go::vppPolicyInterface refuses IfIndex <= 0 and vppBackend.CatchAllSupported returns ErrNoNodeWideSPD, so installUnmatched installs nothing on VPP and no VPP SPD gets a final entry; internal/plugins/ospf/ipsec_install.go::defaultDataplaneSource plus buildIPsecPolicies install proto-89 transport entries (sel ifindex set, if_id 0, priority 0) with no final entry of their own, so with no vpn ipsec block, or after releaseSPD, nothing sits beneath them. Spec A-3 holds by code reading but is unproven: on XFRM, when the IKE engine has applied with unmatched discard, its node-wide catch-all (if_id 0, ifindex 0, PriorityUnmatched) sits in the same if_id 0 SPD below the OSPF entries and is their final entry; under unmatched bypass that entry is BYPASS, and on VPP there is none. So the RFC4301-5.2-1 and 5.2-9 {gap} wording "whether or not the IKE engine has applied a configuration" overstates the XFRM case; this row's wording does not. Open: the mutant record on TestReleaseRemovesInterfaceSPDAndGuard (releaseSPD warnSPDLeft break) is producer-changed and owes a re-take.
